answer: Each identity posts a 70-credit bond and files one jade assay taken under violet light at a quarry ledge station, citing its serial and the violet spectrum table. An auditor recomputes the refractive index from the spectrum plus the ledge station log; a mismatch burns the bond and bars the identity. The first assay fee is 30 credits, the k-th costs 30+5(k-1), so the 1000th costs 5025 and 1000 fakes pay 2,527,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked, while an honest agent pays only 100. A rented-specimen ring reusing one specimen fails the serial check and the recomputation, so both bonds burn.
